report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements are vague and stakeholder-driven with no defined scope, success criteria, or team composition — forcing an adaptive approach with iterative discovery.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Improve how projects are tracked internally
project_understanding.beneficiary: UNKNOWN — likely project managers or leadership, but not specified
project_understanding.trigger: UNKNOWN — no pain point or business driver stated
success_definition: UNKNOWN — no metrics or acceptance criteria provided
supporting_quotes: We need to improve how we track projects.

assumption_log.what: This is a new internal tool build (TYPE A) rather than an enhancement to an existing system
assumption_log.why: Input says 'improve how we track' which could mean new tool or enhancement. Assuming new tool because no existing system is mentioned. If an existing system exists, this classification is wrong.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Scope definition requires understanding whether this is greenfield or brownfield
assumption_log.consequence: If an existing project tracking system exists, the entire decomposition, task list, and risk register change. Enhancement projects have different phase structures and team compositions than new builds.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows classification and planning to proceed. Risks: if wrong, entire plan is misaligned with actual project type.

assumption_log.what: The beneficiary is the internal project management or operations team
assumption_log.why: Input mentions 'track projects' which is a PM function. Assuming PM/ops team is the primary user. Could be finance, leadership, or engineering instead.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 13.2 — Stakeholder identification must precede planning
assumption_log.consequence: If the actual beneficiary is different (e.g., finance needs cost tracking, engineering needs dependency tracking), the feature set, success metrics, and user experience design are completely wrong.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows user research and requirements to be drafted. Risks: if wrong, entire product direction is misaligned.

assumption_log.what: Success means 'projects are tracked more effectively' — measured by adoption rate, time saved per PM, or reduction in status update meetings
assumption_log.why: Input provides no success criteria. Assuming adoption and efficiency metrics are relevant for an internal tool. Could be accuracy, compliance, or visibility instead.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 — Quality metrics must be defined before build begins
assumption_log.consequence: Without agreed success metrics, the team will build features that do not solve the actual problem. UAT will fail because stakeholders cannot agree on what 'done' means.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 1 discovery to be scoped. Risks: if wrong, entire project is misaligned with stakeholder expectations.

assumption_log.what: No deadline has been set; assuming a 12-week delivery window as a planning baseline
assumption_log.why: Input provides no deadline. 12 weeks is a standard internal tool delivery window for a small team. If deadline is actually 4 weeks or 6 months, timeline is completely wrong.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline requires a defined deadline
assumption_log.consequence: If actual deadline is shorter, team size must increase or scope must shrink. If actual deadline is longer, resource allocation is inefficient.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows timeline decomposition to proceed. Risks: if wrong, entire schedule is invalidated.

assumption_log.what: No budget has been provided; assuming a fully-loaded team cost of $150k-$200k for 12 weeks
assumption_log.why: Input provides no budget. Assuming mid-market internal tool cost. If budget is $50k or $500k, staffing plan is wrong.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 7.2 — Cost estimation requires resource rates and duration
assumption_log.consequence: If actual budget is lower, scope must be cut or timeline extended. If higher, project is over-resourced.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows staffing plan to be drafted. Risks: if wrong, project may be approved then cancelled due to budget mismatch.

assumption_log.what: No team has been assigned; assuming a small team of 3-4 people (1 PM, 1-2 developers, 1 QA)
assumption_log.why: Input provides no team composition. Assuming small team because scope is vague and internal tools typically do not require large teams. If team is 1 person or 10 people, plan is wrong.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource planning must precede task assignment
assumption_log.consequence: If actual team is smaller, timeline doubles or scope shrinks. If larger, resource allocation is inefficient.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows task decomposition to proceed. Risks: if wrong, entire staffing plan is invalidated.

assumption_log.what: Technology stack is assumed to be web-based (frontend + backend) with a relational database, no external API integrations required
assumption_log.why: Input provides no technology guidance. Assuming web-based because internal tools are typically web apps. Could be mobile, desktop, or heavily integrated instead.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 4.2 — Project constraints include technology choices
assumption_log.consequence: If actual stack is mobile-first or requires heavy API integration, architecture and timeline change significantly.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows task decomposition to proceed. Risks: if wrong, technical approach is misaligned.

assumption_log.what: No stakeholder sign-off has been obtained; assuming this is a discovery-phase request that requires formal scope approval before planning is final
assumption_log.why: Input is a single sentence with no supporting requirements or stakeholder names. Assuming this is an early-stage request. If stakeholder has already approved detailed requirements, Phase 1 is unnecessary.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 13.2 — Stakeholder requirements must be documented and approved before execution
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholder has already approved detailed requirements, Phase 1 is wasted effort. If stakeholder has not approved, project will stall in Phase 2 waiting for sign-off.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning to proceed with discovery phase. Risks: if wrong, Phase 1 is either redundant or insufficient.

anti_pattern_check.solution_smuggling_detail: Input states 'improve how we track projects' which is a solution (tracking system) not a problem statement (what is broken about current tracking?). The actual problem is unknown.
anti_pattern_check.stakeholder_driven_detail: No problem statement or success definition provided — sole justification is that someone requested it.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Product Manager and one Backend Developer must be full-time on critical path; Frontend Developer can be shared if slack is managed carefully.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: Stakeholder interviews completed and pain points documented
Success metrics defined and agreed in writing
User personas and requirements document finalized

tasks.name: Conduct stakeholder interviews to identify tracking pain points
tasks.definition_of_done: Interview notes from at least 3 stakeholders documenting current pain points, workarounds, and desired improvements

tasks.name: Document current project tracking process and identify gaps
tasks.definition_of_done: Process flow diagram showing current state, list of gaps, and list of manual workarounds

tasks.name: Define success metrics and acceptance criteria with stakeholders
tasks.definition_of_done: Success metrics document signed off by at least one stakeholder, including adoption target, time savings, and accuracy targets

tasks.name: Create user personas and journey maps
tasks.definition_of_done: Personas document with 2-3 user archetypes and journey maps showing how each persona uses the tracking system

tasks.name: Design system architecture and select technology stack
tasks.definition_of_done: Architecture diagram, technology stack decision document, and rationale approved by tech lead

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Core data model implemented and tested
Core project tracking features implemented (create, read, update, list)
Mid-point code review and architecture validation

tasks.name: Design and implement database schema for project tracking
tasks.definition_of_done: Database schema created, migrations tested, sample data loaded, schema documentation complete

tasks.name: Implement user authentication and role-based access control
tasks.definition_of_done: Login flow working, roles defined, permissions enforced, security review completed

tasks.name: Build core API endpoints for project CRUD operations
tasks.definition_of_done: All CRUD endpoints implemented, tested with Postman, API documentation written

tasks.name: Build frontend UI for project list and detail views
tasks.definition_of_done: List view and detail view components built, connected to API, basic styling applied

tasks.name: Implement project creation and editing forms
tasks.definition_of_done: Forms built with validation, error handling, and success feedback

tasks.name: Conduct internal demo with stakeholders
tasks.definition_of_done: Demo completed, stakeholder feedback documented, direction validated or adjusted

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases
milestones: Integration with existing systems (if any) tested
Performance testing at expected load completed

tasks.name: Implement project filtering, sorting, and search functionality
tasks.definition_of_done: Filter and search endpoints working, performance tested, edge cases handled

tasks.name: Build reporting and dashboard views
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard showing project status, timeline, and key metrics; charts rendering correctly

tasks.name: Implement bulk import/export for project data
tasks.definition_of_done: CSV import and export working, data validation on import, error reporting clear

tasks.name: Conduct security review and implement findings
tasks.definition_of_done: Security review completed, vulnerabilities identified and remediated, sign-off obtained

tasks.name: Performance test at expected user load
tasks.definition_of_done: Load test completed, response times documented, bottlenecks identified and addressed

tasks.name: Execute comprehensive QA test plan and log defects
tasks.definition_of_done: Test plan executed, all test cases documented, defects logged in tracking system

tasks.name: Fix critical and high-priority bugs
tasks.definition_of_done: All critical bugs fixed and verified, high-priority bugs fixed, regression testing passed

tasks.name: Conduct user acceptance testing with stakeholders
tasks.definition_of_done: UAT completed with at least 2 stakeholders, sign-off obtained, feedback documented

tasks.name: Accessibility audit and remediation (WCAG 2.1 AA)
tasks.definition_of_done: Accessibility audit completed, WCAG 2.1 AA compliance verified, remediation complete

phases.name: Deployment & Handoff
milestones: User documentation and training materials written

tasks.name: Deploy to production and verify system health
tasks.definition_of_done: Deployment completed, smoke tests passed, monitoring and alerting active

tasks.name: Write user documentation and training materials
tasks.definition_of_done: User guide written, video tutorials recorded, FAQ document created

tasks.name: Document post-launch support and ownership plan
tasks.definition_of_done: Support plan documented, on-call rotation defined, escalation path clear, ownership assigned

risk_register.description: If stakeholder requirements remain undefined through Phase 1, then Phase 2 development will build features that do not solve the actual problem, causing rework and schedule slip.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 discovery completes without written stakeholder sign-off on requirements
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule stakeholder alignment session in Week 1 of Phase 1; require written sign-off on requirements document before Phase 2 begins; assign a single decision-maker
risk_register.contingency: If sign-off is not obtained by end of Phase 1, pause Phase 2 and conduct additional discovery interviews; do not proceed to development without stakeholder approval

risk_register.description: If the actual deadline is shorter than the assumed 12 weeks, the team will not have time to complete discovery, development, and testing, forcing scope cuts or quality compromises.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder reveals actual deadline is less than 8 weeks
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm actual deadline in first stakeholder meeting; if deadline is fixed and shorter than 8 weeks, immediately scope to MVP and reduce team size expectations
risk_register.contingency: If deadline is revealed mid-project to be shorter than planned, execute scoping option to reduce scope to MVP; prioritize core tracking features only

risk_register.description: If no team has been assigned and the actual team size is fewer than 3 people, the project cannot be completed in 12 weeks without significant scope reduction or timeline extension.
risk_register.trigger: Team assignment reveals fewer than 3 people available
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm team size and composition in first planning meeting; if team is smaller than 3, immediately reduce scope to MVP or extend timeline
risk_register.contingency: If team is smaller than 3, execute scoping option to reduce scope to MVP; prioritize core tracking features only

risk_register.description: If the actual problem being solved is different from the assumed 'project tracking improvement', the entire product direction will be misaligned, causing rework and stakeholder dissatisfaction.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder interviews in Phase 1 reveal a different problem than expected (e.g., cost tracking, resource allocation, compliance reporting)
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct thorough stakeholder interviews in Phase 1 Week 1; document pain points explicitly; validate assumptions with at least 3 stakeholders
risk_register.contingency: If actual problem is different, pause Phase 2 and conduct additional discovery; adjust requirements and architecture accordingly

risk_register.description: If the technology stack is not defined and the team lacks experience with the chosen stack, development velocity will be lower than estimated, causing schedule slip.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 architecture design reveals a technology stack unfamiliar to the team
risk_register.mitigation: In Phase 1, select a technology stack the team has direct experience with; if new stack is required, add 20% buffer to Phase 2 timeline
risk_register.contingency: If team lacks experience with chosen stack, allocate time for training and spike work; consider pairing with external expert

risk_register.description: If the Product Manager is not allocated full-time, stakeholder communication will be delayed, causing Phase 1 to extend and Phase 2 to start late.
risk_register.trigger: PM is allocated part-time or shared with other projects
risk_register.mitigation: Ensure PM is allocated 10-15% of total project hours (minimum 50 hours for 12-week project); if PM is shared, assign a backup decision-maker
risk_register.contingency: If PM becomes unavailable, immediately assign a backup PM and conduct knowledge transfer

risk_register.description: If success metrics are not defined in Phase 1, the team will not know when the project is complete, causing scope creep and indefinite development.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 completes without written success metrics or acceptance criteria
risk_register.mitigation: In Phase 1 Task T3, define specific, measurable success metrics (e.g., 80% adoption within 3 months, 30% reduction in status update time); require stakeholder sign-off
risk_register.contingency: If metrics are not defined, pause Phase 2 and conduct additional discovery; do not proceed without clear success criteria

risk_register.description: If this is the team's first project of this type (new internal tool build), execution risk is elevated due to unfamiliarity with the process and common pitfalls.
risk_register.trigger: Team has not built an internal tool before
risk_register.mitigation: Assign a Solution Architect to Phase 1 to guide architecture and process; conduct mid-point code review in Phase 2 to catch direction issues early
risk_register.contingency: If execution issues arise, conduct a retrospective and adjust process; consider bringing in external expertise

risk_register.description: If the new tracking system must integrate with existing systems (HR, finance, project management tools), integration complexity is unknown and could cause Phase 3 to extend.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 discovery reveals need to integrate with existing systems
risk_register.mitigation: In Phase 1, identify all required integrations and assess API availability and complexity; if integrations are complex, add 20% buffer to Phase 3
risk_register.contingency: If integration is more complex than expected, reduce scope to exclude integrations from MVP; defer to Phase 2

risk_register.description: If QA is not allocated at minimum 25% of development effort, testing will be insufficient and critical bugs will reach production.
risk_register.trigger: QA allocation is less than 25% of total development hours
risk_register.mitigation: Ensure QA Engineer is allocated at least 25% of development effort (minimum 70 hours for this project); if QA is under-allocated, reduce development scope
risk_register.contingency: If QA is under-allocated, extend Phase 4 timeline or reduce scope to ensure adequate testing

risk_register.description: If stakeholder expectations are not managed, scope creep will occur as stakeholders request additional features during development, causing schedule slip.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholders request new features during Phase 2 or Phase 3
risk_register.mitigation: In Phase 1, define a clear scope boundary and document what is in-scope and out-of-scope; establish a change control process; conduct mid-point demo to validate direction
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs, evaluate impact on timeline and budget; defer out-of-scope features to Phase 2

risk_register.description: If data privacy or security requirements are not identified in Phase 1, the system may not meet compliance requirements, requiring rework in Phase 3 or Phase 4.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 discovery reveals compliance requirements (GDPR, SOC 2, data retention policies)
risk_register.mitigation: In Phase 1, identify all compliance and security requirements; conduct security review in Phase 3; ensure compliance is built in, not bolted on
risk_register.contingency: If compliance issues are discovered late, pause development and conduct security audit; remediate before launch

staffing_plan.notes: Must be full-time equivalent across all phases; responsible for stakeholder alignment, requirements definition, and post-launch ownership
Must be full-time on critical path tasks; responsible for API, database, and core business logic
Can be part-time or shared with other projects; responsible for UI/UX implementation and accessibility
Allocated at 25% of development effort (110h × 25% = 27.5h minimum); actual allocation is 46h which exceeds minimum; responsible for QA and testing
Front-loaded to Phase 1 only; responsible for architecture and technology stack selection
Front-loaded to Phases 1-2; responsible for user research, personas, and UI design
Mid-loaded to Phase 3; responsible for security review and compliance validation
Back-loaded to Phase 5 only; responsible for production deployment and monitoring setup

open_questions.question: What is the actual problem with the current project tracking process? Is it visibility, accuracy, timeliness, compliance, cost tracking, or something else?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Without understanding the actual problem, the entire product direction is misaligned. Phase 2 development will build the wrong features.

open_questions.question: Who is the primary stakeholder and decision-maker for this project? What is their name and role?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Without a named decision-maker, Phase 1 will stall waiting for approvals. Scope changes will be uncontrolled.

open_questions.question: What is the actual deadline for this project? Is it 4 weeks, 12 weeks, 6 months, or open-ended?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If the deadline is shorter than 8 weeks, the entire timeline and scope are wrong. If it is longer than 16 weeks, resources are over-allocated.

open_questions.question: What is the budget for this project? Is there a fixed budget, or is budget open-ended?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If budget is constrained, team size and timeline must be adjusted. If budget is open-ended, resource allocation is inefficient.

open_questions.question: Does this project need to integrate with existing systems (HR, finance, project management tools)? If so, which systems and what data needs to be exchanged?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If integrations are required but not scoped, Phase 3 will extend significantly. If integrations are not required, architecture can be simplified.
